external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who opens the dispatch console in a browser.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network. They open the dispatch console in their browser.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: A scheduling partner company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript app used by duty engineers and connected to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The host that serves the dispatch console application.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the console and schedule importer, which reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: An hourly importer that retrieves and parses the scheduling partner's SOAP feed and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token. That token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: Database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order in it carries the token or the session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder where the importer writes each downloaded scheduling document.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_stores.name: corporate file store
data_stores.description: The corporate file store containing the schedule archive folder.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store

data_flows.name: load console
data_flows.description: The duty engineer loads the dispatch console from the corporate web host.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser. ... our corporate web host serves it.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and the API are served from different origins, so the API answers the console cross-origin. The permitted origins and credential setting were not recorded.

data_flows.name: open WebSocket
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and maintains a WebSocket connection to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether that socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after it is open.

data_flows.name: read and write database
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads from and writes to the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull planned work
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's planned work feed.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies our importer, or how our importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls. It presents an API token.
data_flows.notes: The token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers sit and the schedule importer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company control-plane zone holding the live estate, with authority to move a crew and change depot work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: A corporate laptop holds none of those rights. The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the scheduling partner, which is another company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database's data is confidential because it contains crew names, crew mobile numbers, job orders, and tokens or sessions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database holds job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
